# 06 — API Surface & Client Contracts

## 1. Executive summary (top 5 findings, one line each)

1. **The MCP HTTP transport is an open proxy**: with `MEMONGO_API_KEY` set (which it must be for the proxy to work), `refuseToServeOpen` passes and the unauthenticated `/mcp` endpoint proxies authenticated upstream memory reads/writes to anyone with network reach (apps/mcp/src/http-transport.ts:69-73).
2. **The client SDK retries non-idempotent mutations on 503**: `apiFetch` retries every POST on 429/503, but only `add`/`writeEvent`/`writeEvents` carry idempotency keys — lifecycle update/delete, feedback, procedure outcome, self-edit, and extract can double-apply on a mid-flight 503 (packages/client/src/client.ts:137, 195-222, 778-830).
3. **`/v1/search-detailed` type-casts five nested objects into the engine with zero field validation** (`structuredScope`, `referenceScope`, `proceduralScope`, `conversationScope`, `searchConfig`), the last unvalidated boundary on an otherwise strictly-validated API (apps/api/src/routes/v1-search-routes.ts:193-277).
4. **Version-skew telemetry is dead code**: the client sends `x-memongo-client-version` on every request and the status route comments that clients can "detect version skew", but no server code ever reads the header — no log, no warning, no rejection (packages/client/src/client.ts:176-177; apps/api/src/routes/v1-status-routes.ts:73-75).
5. **`mode: "full"` is silently dropped by `/v1/context-bundle`** while the client SDK types, MCP tool schema, and tools package all declare `enum ["full","wake-up"]` — and any other invalid mode value is silently swallowed instead of rejected (apps/api/src/routes/v1-context-routes.ts:139 vs apps/mcp/src/tools/core.ts:414-416).

## 3. Correctness bugs (reasoned reproductions)

**B1 — MCP HTTP transport is an unauthenticated proxy (severity: security).**
`startHttpTransport` treats `Boolean(process.env.MEMONGO_API_KEY)` as the auth signal for `refuseToServeOpen(host, hasApiKey)` (apps/mcp/src/http-transport.ts:69-73). But the API key authenticates the *upstream* `MemongoClient`; the `/mcp` endpoint itself performs no auth of its own (the request handler at lines 76-93 checks only the URL path). Reproduction: deploy `MEMONGO_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0 MEMONGO_API_KEY=sk-... memongo-mcp --http`; the guardrail passes (key present); any host that can reach port 3110 gets the full tool surface (search, write, lifecycle delete, self-edit) executed with the server's credentials. Additionally the 500 fallback at lines 84-92 returns raw `err.message` to the caller — internal error disclosure. (Also tracked by category 05; listed here because it is the MCP client contract.)

**B2 — Client retries non-idempotent mutations on 429/503 (severity: double-apply).**
`shouldRetryStatus` returns true for 429/503 and `apiFetch` retries *any* method (packages/client/src/client.ts:137, 210-215). All mutating calls go through `apiPost` → `apiFetch`. Only `add`, `writeEvent`, `writeEvents` attach an `Idempotency-Key` (client.ts:633, 884, 924). `updateLifecycleItem` (client.ts:778), `deleteLifecycleItem` (client.ts:789), `reportProcedureOutcome` (client.ts:805), `applyMemoryFeedback` (client.ts:816), `extract` (client.ts:951), and `selfEdit` (client.ts:1273) send none. Reproduction: server accepts `/v1/lifecycle/update`, the write lands in MongoDB, then a proxy (or a dependency-unavailable path after mutation) returns 503; the client sleeps and re-POSTs the same patch; the item gains an extra revision and `reportProcedureOutcome` increments success/failure counters twice. Note 429 retries are safe (request never processed); 503-after-write is the dangerous case.

**B3 — `/v1/search-detailed` nested objects are type-cast, not validated (severity: query-shape injection into engine).**
Lines 193-277 of apps/api/src/routes/v1-search-routes.ts cast `sourcePreference` (array check only), `conversationScope` (object check only), `structuredScope`, `referenceScope`, `proceduralScope` (object-null checks only), and `searchConfig` (object-null-nonArray check only) straight into the bridge call with `as` casts. Unknown/operator-shaped keys pass through untouched into MongoDB query construction — the exact class of bug `kbFilterSchema` (`.strict()`) and `metadataSchema` (`$`/dot key rejection) were built to prevent at apps/api/src/lib/validation.ts:83-107. Reproduction: `POST /v1/search-detailed {"query":"x","structuredScope":{"$where":"..."}}` returns 200 with the object accepted, versus `POST /v1/search-kb {"filter":{"$where":"..."}}` which is rejected 400. Whether the engine ultimately *evaluates* operator keys depends on the aggregation path, but the API contract is inconsistent: one search route validates, its sibling does not.

**B4 — `mode` contract drift + silent invalid-value swallow on `/v1/context-bundle`.**
The API maps `mode: body.mode === "wake-up" ? "wake-up" : undefined` (apps/api/src/routes/v1-context-routes.ts:139) — `"full"` and every invalid value alike become "default". But the client SDK types accept `mode` and forward it verbatim (packages/client/src/client.ts:1019-1039), the MCP tool declares `enum: ["full","wake-up"]` (apps/mcp/src/tools/core.ts:414-416), and the tools package declares `z.enum(["full","wake-up"])` (packages/tools/src/index.ts:100). Reproduction: an agent sends `mode: "wakeup"` (typo) via MCP — schema validation rejects it at a strict host, but a lenient host or direct API call returns a full default bundle with 200, no error. Every other enum on this API returns 400 (`discoveryKind` at v1-context-routes.ts:90-95 does exactly that in the same handler). `"full"` being accepted-but-ignored is at least self-consistent (default == full) but misleading to callers who think they toggled something.

**B5 — Chain-trace returns a fabricated success for an invalid collection (severity: silent failure).**
The route validates only that `collection` is a non-empty string (apps/api/src/routes/v1-maintenance-routes.ts:22-28); the engine then checks `COLLECTION_ID_FIELDS[collection]` and returns `emptyResult` — `nodes: []`, **`chainComplete: true`** — for any unknown collection (packages/memory-engine/src/mongodb-reasoning-chain.ts:34, 74-84). Reproduction: `POST /v1/chain-trace {"factId":"<real id>","collection":"structured_memories"}` (a plausible-but-wrong name) returns 200 with an empty-but-"complete" chain. A caller auditing provenance cannot distinguish "no premises exist" from "you named the collection wrong". Same swallow exists in the tools package where `collection: z.string()` has no enum (packages/tools/src/index.ts:411).

**B6 — MCP `memongo_write_structured` type enum is narrower than the API it fronts.**
The MCP schema restricts `entry.type` to a 14-value enum (apps/mcp/src/tools/core.ts:227-241) while the API's `structuredEntrySchema` accepts any non-empty string (`type: z.string().trim().min(1)`, apps/api/src/lib/validation.ts:47) and the engine treats type as open-ended. Reproduction: a client writes `{"type":"relationship",...}` successfully via `@memongo/client`; the same write via MCP is rejected by any schema-enforcing host (or passes unvalidated at lenient hosts — either way the surfaces disagree). Pick one contract: open string everywhere, or enum everywhere (and if enum, validate it server-side too).

**B7 — Admin `memoryIds` comma-splitting corrupts/cannot express IDs containing commas.**
`memoryIdsRaw.split(",")` (apps/api/src/routes/v1-admin-routes.ts:85-88, 114-117) with no escaping and no per-ID format validation. Any present or future ID format containing a comma is silently split into two bogus IDs that match nothing (or worse, match the wrong documents after trim). GET query params make this awkward, but a repeated-parameter form (`?memoryIds=a&memoryIds=b`) or POST body solves it. Low likelihood today (IDs are ObjectId/UUID-shaped) — filed as a latent contract trap, not an active bug.

## 4. Unknown unknowns (things no checklist covers — HIGHEST VALUE)

**U1 — Auto-generated idempotency keys protect transport retries only, and cost permanent storage.**
The client generates a fresh UUIDv4 per *call* (`input.customId ?? generateIdempotencyKey()`, client.ts:617, 866, 924). Consequence 1: an application-level double-submit (the classic "user double-clicks, agent retries its own tool call") produces a *new* key and is **not** deduped — the guarantee the docs imply ("a replay returns the original receipt") holds only inside one client call's retry loop. Consequence 2: because every SDK write now carries a key, the engine persists a SHA-256 fingerprint + unique-indexed key on *every* event document forever (mongodb-manager-write.ts:543-548) — Stripe expires idempotency records after 24h; memongo has no TTL on them, so the events collection carries a permanently growing unique index of one-time UUIDs. The MCP tools do expose `customId` as the app-level key (core.ts `memongo_add`/`memongo_write_event` schemas) — but the tools package's `addSchema`/`writeEventSchema` omit it entirely (packages/tools/src/index.ts:47-68), so AI-SDK integrations cannot set it at all.

**U2 — Silent mode masks *auth* failures as empty memory.**
`_silently` degrades every read failure — including 401/403 — to an empty result (client.ts:64-68, 598-603; writes are excluded, reads never report). An agent deployed with a revoked or mistyped API key will believe the memory store is simply empty and answer confidently from a blank slate; there is no counter, log hook, or distinction between "unavailable" and "unauthorized". This directly contradicts the repo's own anti-silent-failure guardrail philosophy (refuseToServeOpen, tripwires) — the guardrails refuse to serve open, but the client refuses to *report* closed.

**U3 — No continuation mechanism on any list route.**
Every list endpoint is top-N only: admin lists cap at 100 (v1-helpers.ts:15, 70-78), lifecycle history at 200 (v1-helpers.ts:16), jobs at 100 — and none accept an offset, cursor, or return a total or next-page token. A caller cannot enumerate all traces or all jobs; they can only ever see the first page. For an agent iterating its own revision history past 200 entries there is no API path at all. This is beyond "pagination consistency" — it's pagination absence with caps as the mitigation.

**U4 — Lifecycle handles are fat structured objects the LLM must echo verbatim.**
The lifecycle contract requires round-tripping a handle containing `family, id, agentId, scope, scopeRef, revision, state, structured.{type,key}` (packages/tools/src/index.ts:110-150 documents it; apps/mcp/src/tools/aliases.ts describes the fields *only in description text* with schema `type: object` and zero properties). Competitors use a flat opaque string ID (mem0's `memory_id`). Token cost per feedback/update call is large, and one hallucinated field (e.g. stale `revision`) yields a 403 identity mismatch (lifecycleHandleIdentityError) the model must debug. A server-issued opaque handle string that the API resolves would shrink every call.

**U5 — No deprecation mechanism anywhere in the contract.**
No Sunset headers, no deprecation logging, no field-level deprecation markers in the OpenAPI document — nothing a client can programmatically detect. With 4 active surfaces (API, client, MCP, tools) already drifting (§3), there is no protocol for retiring a field on one surface without silently breaking another. mem0 logs deprecation warnings for legacy top-level fields in `/search` (server/main.py:452-462); the OpenAPI spec has `deprecated` flags memongo could set for free.

**U6 — POST-only RPC API gives up HTTP semantics without gaining anything.**
29 of 41 routes are POST, including pure reads (`/lifecycle/get`, `/search`) and idempotent-by-construction deletes (`/lifecycle/delete` is invalidate-with-history — safe to repeat — yet POST). Cost: no HTTP caching, no conditional requests, and every "GET-shaped" call consumes a rate-limit token as a write. The safety rationale (all mutations POST) is already violated by POST-shaped `/sync` and GET `/probes/*` being state-changing/dependent (v1-status-routes.ts:101, 115, 125). REST verbs plus the existing envelope would be strictly more expressive; this is a deliberate style choice worth revisiting before v2 freezes it.

## 6. External docs alignment (MongoDB/MCP/OWASP where relevant)

- **MCP Streamable HTTP transport (modelcontextprotocol.io)**: memongo instantiates a fresh `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` per request (http-transport.ts:44-60) — correct for the stateless mode the SDK supports. However the MCP spec's security guidance for local servers recommends validating the `Origin` header (DNS-rebinding protection) and, when authorization is enabled, returning `401` with `WWW-Authenticate`; memongo's transport does neither — it has no auth at all (B1) and no Origin check on the request path (http-transport.ts:76-93 checks only the pathname). **Misaligned.**
- **IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header**: header-takes-precedence-over-body is implemented and documented exactly per the draft (v1-helpers.ts:306-315; openapi-schemas.ts `Idempotency-Key` header parameter); key-reuse-with-different-payload → 422 matches Stripe's semantics (mongodb-manager-write.ts:489). One deviation: the draft/Stripe model scopes replay to a retention window (24h); memongo replays forever (U1). **Mostly aligned.**
- **OpenAPI 3 (spec.openapis.org)**: the document is generated in TS and *enforced* against the live route table, required/optional field sets, header parameters, error statuses, bearer scheme, and canonical scope enums by contract-conformance.test.ts:82-290. This is stronger conformance than most hand-written specs. **Aligned.** (The OpenAPI documents `Idempotency-Key` but not `x-memongo-client-version` — consistent with the server never reading it.)
- **OWASP LLM (sensitive disclosure)**: the HTTP API's error envelope never leaks stacks, queries, or connection strings (errors.ts; internalError passes only a requestId); the one leak is the MCP HTTP transport's 500 handler echoing `err.message` (http-transport.ts:84-92) — and agent-memory's own code comments note that driver errors quote connection strings, so the same class of risk applies to whatever the transport catches. **One violation on the MCP surface.**

## 7. Recommendations (P0 = data loss/security, P1 = correctness/cost, P2 = quality)

**P0**
1. Close the MCP HTTP transport auth hole (B1): require a token (env-provided or per-key) on `/mcp` before proxying, and stop treating upstream `MEMONGO_API_KEY` presence as endpoint auth. Add Origin/Host validation per MCP spec. Redact the 500 fallback to a generic message.

**P1**
2. Stop retrying non-idempotent mutations (B2): either restrict `apiFetch` retries to requests carrying an `Idempotency-Key`, or give lifecycle update/delete/feedback/procedure-outcome/self-edit/extract handle+revision-based natural idempotency (CAS on revision) server-side.
3. Validate `/v1/search-detailed` nested objects with zod schemas mirroring `kbFilterSchema` strictness (B3); same for the `timeRange` casts in v1-context-routes.ts:103-110, 127-135.
4. Resolve the `mode` drift (B4): validate `mode` as an enum at the API (400 on invalid), and either honor or remove `"full"` across client types, MCP schema, and tools schema in the same change.
5. Make version skew real (B4/header): log or warn when `x-memongo-client-version` differs from `MEMONGO_API_VERSION` on the server, or delete the header and the misleading comments. Cheapest high-trust win on the list.
6. Return 400 from `/v1/chain-trace` for collections outside the engine allowlist (B5) — the route should own the enum the engine already enforces; mirror it in the tools package `collection` schema.

**P2**
7. Unify the write-structured `type` contract (B6): open string or enum, consistently across API validation, MCP schema, and tools package; type the alias tools' `handle`/`patch` schemas (the tools package already has correct zod handle schemas at packages/tools/src/index.ts:110-150 — port them to the MCP server).
8. Trim `@memongo/memory` to re-export `@memongo/memory-bridge` only, or a curated allowlist (checklist 9; packages/memongo-memory/src/index.ts:2).
9. Add a deprecation protocol (U5): OpenAPI `deprecated` flags + a `Sunset` header + a mem0-style server log line when a deprecated field is used.
10. Expose `customId`/`metadata`/`expiresAt` in the tools package `add`/`writeEvent` schemas (U1; packages/tools/src/index.ts:47-68) so AI-SDK callers get the idempotency and TTL contract the other three surfaces have; align `searchKbSchema` with `filter`; replace `z.string()` with enums for salience/temporalScope (packages/tools/src/index.ts:174-175).
11. Make silent mode distinguish 401/403 (throw or surface a counter) from availability failures (U2), and document that auto idempotency keys cover transport retries only; consider a TTL policy for stored fingerprints (U1).
12. Add a continuation mechanism to list routes (U3) — even a simple `offset` or `nextCursor` on admin lists and lifecycle history; replace `memoryIds` comma-splitting with repeated query params (B7).
13. Consider an unauthenticated, counters-only `/healthz` (agent-memory pattern) so probes work during incidents; `/v1/status` can stay authenticated.

Verification status: everything above was verified by reading executing source (no docs trusted; repo at commit 1d98eb36f1, clean tree). Not verified / out of scope: runtime behavior of MongoDB query construction for operator-shaped keys inside `structuredScope` (B3 states the contract inconsistency, not a proven injection); end-to-end load behavior of rate-limiter buckets (fail-closed logic read only); the `letta` competitor was excluded per its repository's own AGENTS.md policy (landing-page repo, archived server off-limits for comparison); `getzep/zep` and `langchain-ai/langmem` REST surfaces were not directly inspected (langmem has no REST server; zep not cloned in the competitor set).
